I am an old man now, and my bones are not what they used to be, but I still know this land. I will put a small amount of chemical fertilizer on my maize—perhaps what I can get from the subsidy program—because the soil is tired, and I will also spread manure from my goats to help it. I will plant the improved maize seed again, as it gives me better food for my grandchildren, but I will not waste money on sprays or irrigation when the rains come and my family can pull the weeds by hand. My sons and their children will do most of the work on this small plot, and we do not have cash to hire anyone from the village.
